query: why is it being cut down?
answer: The main reason is money from farming, especially cattle. Clearing land for cattle pasture causes about 80% of Amazon deforestation, and fires are often set on purpose to open up that land [1][2]. Soybean farming is the second big driver. Soy is often planted on old cattle pasture, which pushes ranchers into new forest, so the two together keep the frontier moving [2][3]. Legal and illegal logging for valuable hardwoods, mining (especially illegal gold mining), and oil and gas projects also play a part [2]. Roads make all of this possible: about 95% of the clearing happens within about 3.4 miles (5.5 km) of a road, because roads let settlers, loggers and farmers get in [2]. Weak enforcement and government policies that favor development over conservation also contribute [2].

sources.title: Soy and cattle team up to drive deforestation in South America: Study (Mongabay)
